label: Captain America
description: Earnest, steady and encouraging, and he can do this all day.
direction: Speak warm, steady and earnest, a clear confident baritone with old-fashioned decency and quiet leadership. Calm and encouraging, never barking. Keep the direction word crisp.
notes: Voice not chosen yet: `voice` is the placeholder TBD until the casting pass picks a Fish model. The film-era Steve Rogers register: a decent man giving orders kindly. Catchphrases sit on greetings and road prompts; turns stay plain.

rights.author: Marvel (character created by Joe Simon and Jack Kirby)
rights.pd_basis: None. Marvel, owned by Disney, holds copyright and trademark in the character. The register here is the film portrayal by Chris Evans, who is living.
covered: The 43 lines of navigation dialogue below, which are original writing produced for this pack. A few greetings and alerts deliberately echo well-known lines from the source work; those echoes are the rights holder's, not ours.
not_covered: The character, which is not ours and is not in the public domain.
The character's name, which is a live trademark.
Any recorded voice performance of the character, including Chris Evans's.

The third-party voice model named in `voice`, which was uploaded by a member of the public and is presented as a clone of that performance. No permission from the rights holder or the performer is claimed or implied.
Any commercial use. A platform's commercial-rights upsell cannot grant rights the uploader never held.
rights.notes: This preset is in copyright and says so. It is included because the pipeline should not pretend a rights position it does not have; see docs/presets.md before publishing anything built from it. The public-domain presets are pooh, eeyore and tigger.

lines.in_quarter_mile: In a quarter of a mile.
lines.in_1000_meters: In one kilometer. Stay sharp, soldier.
lines.in_1500_meters: In one point five kilometers. Hold the line.
lines.in_one_mile: In one mile. I can do this all day.
lines.start_drive_1: Avengers, assemble! In the car, seat belts on.
lines.start_drive_2: I can do this all day. Let's roll out.
lines.start_drive_3: Suit up, soldier. And by suit, I mean seat belt.
lines.start_drive_4: I was asleep for seventy years. I'm ready for a drive.
lines.start_drive_5: Whatever it takes. Today that means beating the traffic.
lines.start_drive_6: I understood that reference. It was the address. Let's go.
lines.start_drive_7: Language! Sorry, old habit. Let's hit the road.
lines.start_drive_8: Together. That's how we get there. Let's drive.
lines.start_drive_9: I don't like bullies, and I don't like being late. Move out.
lines.exit_left: Take the exit on the left.
lines.exit_right: Take the exit on the right.
lines.u_turn: Make a U turn. No shame in it. We regroup and go again.
lines.arrived: We've arrived. Mission accomplished. Good work, soldier.
lines.exit_fifth: take the fifth exit. I can do this all day.
lines.exit_sixth: take the sixth exit. Hold the line.
lines.exit_seventh: take the seventh exit. Whatever it takes.
lines.traffic_ahead: Traffic ahead. Stand fast. We get through this together.
lines.accident_ahead: An accident ahead. Slow down, and give them room to work.
lines.hazard_ahead: A hazard ahead. Eyes up, soldier.
lines.speed_camera_ahead: Speed camera ahead. The limit is not a suggestion, son.
lines.red_light_camera_ahead: Red light camera ahead. We stop. It's the decent thing to do.
lines.police_ahead: Police ahead. Good people doing a tough job. Ease off.
lines.reroute_chime: Missed it. No problem. We adapt and keep moving.
